beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Fifteen hundred years before Christ, God pulled a shepherd off a mountainside and showed him who He is. What Moses learned up there is everything the famine would later starve out of the world.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You know the story's shape. A bush that burned and was not consumed. Ten plagues. A sea standing on end, and a slave nation walking out of Egypt on dry ground.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: And the Lord spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Face to face. As a man speaks to his friend. Not a force. Not an abstraction. A Person — knowable, present, and shockingly personal.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And in vision, God told Moses what all of it is FOR. One sentence. The mission statement of everything:

beats.speaker: father
beats.text: For behold, this is my work and my glory — to bring to pass the immortality and eternal life of man.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: His work and His glory — is your life. Not His ego. Not His applause. When someone asks why God wants worship, there is the answer: His glory is His children rising. Worship is scaffolding for us. It was never applause for Him.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And Moses learned one more thing on that mountain. Because after the glory withdrew, another voice showed up.

beats.speaker: devil
beats.text: Moses, son of man, worship me.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Son of man. Hear the insult — God had just called him My Son. The devil's first move is always to shrink your title. Now watch what a man who knows who he is does with that:

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: Who art thou? For behold, I am a son of God, in the similitude of his Only Begotten; and where is thy glory, that I should worship thee?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Who art thou — for I am a son of God. That is the whole exchange. A man who has seen God's face and knows his own name cannot be bluffed. The voice raged and the ground shook — and Moses ended it with one sentence:

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: Depart from me, Satan, for this one God only will I worship, which is the God of glory.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And he departed. He always does, eventually, before a child of God standing on their identity. That is not a Moses-only trick. That is the family defense.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Israel walked out of Egypt with that God — fire by night, bread from the sky, water from rock — and still forgot Him within weeks, dancing around a golden calf. And God's answer, for the next thousand years? He kept sending. But that is the next episode.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: For now, keep Moses' two treasures. God has a face. And you have a title: child of God. His whole work and glory is raising you — and nothing that calls you smaller than that speaks for heaven.

card.speaker: narrator
card.text: God has a face. You have a title — child of God. Never let anyone shrink either one.
